title: Adaptive Ramp & Gate Orchestration for Progressive Deploys
creator: Priya Suri
description: Add an orchestration layer and runbook for adaptive traffic ramps and rollout gates that allow safe model/runtime upgrades across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments. Goals: (1) standardized canary + % ramp semantics that integrate with feature flags, (2) automated gate evaluation using SLO/health/quality signals, (3) auto-rollback policies and manual override paths surfaced in Console, and (4) telemetry hooks and dashboards to validate each step.
background: Current progressive delivery tooling is ad hoc: simple static percent ramps (0,10,50,100) driven by CI scripts and manual checks. We've seen two incidents where latency regressed at 30% traffic and a model quality regression slipped through because we lacked automatic quality gating. This ticket aims to build a reusable, programmable rollout engine and default gate configs for model/runtime releases.
proposal: Implement an orchestration service (rollout-controller) that consumes a declarative rollout manifest. The controller runs a state machine: canary -> staged ramps -> full rollout. Each stage evaluates a set of gates: production health metrics (error rate, 95p latency), SLO burn rate over a sliding window, model-quality signals (synthetic eval set PASS/FAIL, sampling-based human verification), and custom feature-flag checks. Ramp schedule is adaptive: start with micro-canary (0.5% requests), then double every interval (0.5% -> 1% -> 2% -> 4% -> 8% -> 16% -> 32%) until target or a gate trips. Gate thresholds are configurable per-project and can be pinned to LTS channels. The controller exposes REST and webhook hooks for Console, alerts, and CI to start/abort rollouts.
rollout_plan: 1) Add rollout-controller skeleton and manifest schema. 2) Implement micro-canary traffic knob in router to support <1% routes. 3) Add gate evaluators: metrics-slo, health-check, quality-eval, anomaly-detection. 4) Wire feature-flag integration so rollout stages can target user cohorts or customers. 5) Implement adaptive ramp algorithm + backoff policy. 6) Integrate auto-rollback action and manual override UI in Console. 7) Create default release profiles and doc runbooks.
acceptance_criteria:
- rollout-controller accepts a manifest and executes a multi-stage rollout.
- default profile can perform a micro-canary starting at 0.5% and reach 100% when gates pass.
- gates evaluate automatically and pause rollouts on threshold breaches within specified time windows.
- auto-rollback triggers on configured SLO breaches and reverts routing within 60s.
- Console surfaces rollout progress, current stage, and provides "Abort" and "Halt" controls.
- E2E tests in CI simulate a regression and verify rollback occurs and alerts fire.
testing_plan: Preflight: unit tests for state machine and gate logic. Integration: local cluster with canary router, wire controller to test metrics backend (Prometheus) and synthetic traffic generator. Staging: run several controlled rollouts against a non-critical model: (a) benign change to validate paths, (b) injected latency regression to validate pause/rollback. Include model-quality gating by running synthetic eval set against canary tokens and a small human review cohort for ambiguous signals.
rollback_strategy: Two-tier rollback: (A) automated immediate rollback when a critical gate trips (SLO burn rate > configured threshold OR error_rate spike > X% over sliding window). Controller will withdraw traffic from canary by 100% within 60s and route back to previous model variant. (B) gradual abort: if non-critical metric drifts but below critical threshold, pause ramp and notify on-call; after manual review operator can continue or roll back. Controller records events in audit log and creates an incident ticket template with link to failed gates and metric diffs.
implementation_notes:
Manifest example (stringified YAML in config store):
---
model: my-model:v2025-03-xx
profile: default-adaptive
stages:
  - name: micro-canary
    target: 0.5
    duration: 10m
    gates: [metrics-slo, quality-eval]
  - name: ramping
    target: 32
    algorithm: adaptive-doubling
    step_interval: 10m
    max_step: 16
    gates: [metrics-slo]
  - name: final
    target: 100
    duration: 30m
    gates: [metrics-slo, post-rollout-quality-check]
Edge cases: support private deployments where Console webhook is unavailable (controller falls back to polling and local audit logs), respect customer pinning for Dedicated/LTS channels.
